leadText:
The Omega Ruby & Alpha Sapphire arc (Japanese: ルビー・ サファイア編 Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire arc), also referred to as The 13th Chapter (Japanese: 第十三章 The Thirteenth Chapter), is the thirteenth story arc of the Pokémon Adventures . It was originally published digitally in Shogakukan's Web Sunday, but moved to Sunday Web Every starting with chapter 20. Chapter 1 was released on January 6, 2015, with subsequent chapters being released individually on the first Tuesday of every month. It began serialization in December 2014, and ended in September 2016.

The arc follows the adventures of , , and as they try and learn the secrets of Mega Evolution to prevent their planet from being destroyed by an incoming meteoroid. Meanwhile, a young woman named Zinnia is out to exact vengeance upon the Devon Corporation for the wrong they did to her people in the past. The arc is roughly based on the events of the Delta Episode of the Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire games.

The Omega Ruby & Alpha Sapphire arc (Japanese: ルビー・ サファイア編 Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire arc), also referred to as The 13th Chapter (Japanese: 第十三章 The Thirteenth Chapter), is the thirteenth story arc of the Pokémon Adventures . It was originally published digitally in Shogakukan's Web Sunday, but moved to Sunday Web Every starting with chapter 20. Chapter 1 was released on January 6, 2015, with subsequent chapters being released individually on the first Tuesday of every month. It began serialization in December 2014, and ended in September 2016.

The arc follows the adventures of , , and as they try and learn the secrets of Mega Evolution to prevent their planet from being destroyed by an incoming meteoroid. Meanwhile, a young woman named Zinnia is out to exact vengeance upon the Devon Corporation for the wrong they did to her people in the past. The arc is roughly based on the events of the Delta Episode of the Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire games.

== Terminology ==
 
This arc gets its name from the core series games, Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire.

==Volumes==

===Mini-volumes===
====Japan====
 
As with the before it, the Omega Ruby & Alpha Sapphire arc was collected separately into mini-volumes. The first volume was released on July 24, 2015, with the final volume released on September 28, 2016.

These volumes have also been localized in English by Shogakukan Asia.

====United States====
 
An English translation of the Omega Ruby & Alpha Sapphire arc was released VIZ Media under the title Pokémon Omega Ruby Alpha Sapphire which was released as their own mini-volumes much like the X & Y arc. The first volume was released on September 6, 2016, with the final volume released on March 6, 2018.

==Chapters==
 

==Important events==
 
 
Three years have passed since the .

==Party changes==
===Evolutions===
The following Pokémon evolve:
Ruby's into Gardevoir (PS596)
Sapphire's into (PS596)

===Releases===
The following Pokémon are released back into the wild:
Ruby's (prior to PS596)
Sapphire's (prior to PS596)

===Mega Evolutions===
The following Pokémon Mega Evolve:
↔ Mega Latios, with Ruby (PS598)
Emerald's ↔ Mega Sceptile (PS599)
Sapphire's Blaziken ↔ Mega Blaziken (PS599)
Ruby's Swampert ↔ Mega Swampert (PS604)
Red's Venusaur ↔ Mega Venusaur (PS607)
Green's Blastoise ↔ Mega Blastoise (PS607)
Sapphire's ↔ Mega Gallade (PS616)
Ruby's Gardevoir ↔ Mega Gardevoir (PS616)
↔ Mega Diancie, with Ruby (PAORAS21)

==Gym Battles==
No Gym Leaders are challenged.

 
==Trivia==
This arc takes place within the same year as the .
At over 1,100 days, this arc has the longest gap in-between the Japanese release dates of Volume 64 and 65.

==Related articles==
